summary:
Charter's newsletter combines new AI research with highlights from its sixth annual Charter Workplace Summit, closing with an interview between CNN host Van Jones and Charter editor-in-chief Kevin Delaney.

AI and Work Radar items: The new Charter AI Pulse, based on surveys of more than 5,000 US desk workers, managers, and executives, finds only about 1 in 10 AI users say the technology is making both their work and lives much better. The strongest predictor of benefiting from AI is agency, meaning having a say in how AI fits into one's job. Executives are twice as likely as workers to trust AI outputs over their own judgment, and 3.3 times as likely to regularly use outputs they doubt. Pew Research Center analysis finds men in highly AI-exposed occupations saw 24% job growth while women's employment growth stayed nearly flat; the pattern reverses in least-exposed occupations. LinkedIn reports AI safety job openings spiked 91% over the past year, with talent described as the main bottleneck. New York governor Kathy Hochul announced a $10 million AI Jobs Institute training center aiming to train up to 40,000 low-income New Yorkers by 2032.

Van Jones, also co-founder of workplace AI coaching platform Rapport, argues workers are stressed, divided, and disengaged because media consumption has become more differentiated across people while each individual's feed is more homogenous, leaving leaders managing people with little in common. He says an earlier experiment turning a Slack channel into daily political argument failed because people lacked the mindset and toolset. He criticizes low tolerance for expressed disagreement, citing graduates equating disagreeable speech with violence. He describes co-hosting Crossfire with Newt Gingrich as transformative, leading him to apologize for stereotyping conservatives and to pass 16 bills together in red states, including on dignity for incarcerated women.
